paragraphs: Swamiji once came across a humorous story in a book and loved to retell it.

An American ship was going down at sea. The sailors, sure that their end had come, wanted one last bit of comfort: some kind of religious service before the waves took them. Luckily, on board was a man they called Uncle Josh, an elder of the Presbyterian Church.
Panicking, they crowded around him and pleaded with him to do something religious, quickly, since they were all about to die.
Uncle Josh rose to the occasion in the only way he seemed to know. He took off his hat and went around collecting money from everyone, right there on the sinking ship!
learn: It's easy to confuse the outward habits of religion, rituals, donations, routines, with its real heart. Ask yourself whether your own practices actually change you, or whether they have become automatic.
